- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml: lines 1361-1397 (the new terminal branch) and lines 1231-1282 (summarize_scoped_impl_runs helper); test assertions at tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_plan_polling_guard.py:654-668 and 670-684 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cycle-local cache `IMPL_SCOPED_ACTIVE_RUN_ID` only covers the rc=0-with-active path. When `summarize_scoped_impl_runs` returns rc=2 (capped walk — every page up to SCOPED_RUN_LOOKUP_MAX_PAGES=10 was full) or rc=1 (unreadable page), the terminal branch only logs a "treating as unknown, waiting" line and clears nothing. The next iteration of the outer `while true` loop therefore re-runs the full helper again, re-reading every page from 1 to 10 on every POLL_INTERVAL tick.
  WHY: With the default POLL_INTERVAL=10s and a typical PHASE_TIMEOUT of tens of minutes for Implement, a persistent capped result drives up to ~6 walks/min × 10 pages = 60 GitHub API calls per minute for one smoke job, all on `actions/runs?created=>${IMPL_CREATED_AFTER}` with the issue-scoped filter applied client-side. Page-1 churn keeps resetting `LAST_ACTIVITY`, so this repeats until PHASE_TIMEOUT or the job deadline. The two existing tests lock the bad behavior in: `test_implement_treats_a_capped_walk_as_unknown_and_reads_at_most_ten_pages` asserts `len(paged) == 20` (two polls × 10 pages), and `test_implement_treats_an_unreadable_page_as_unknown_until_the_inactivity_limit` asserts `sum("&page=2&" in path ...) == 2`. So the regression is not only present but pinned by tests.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml: summarize_scoped_impl_runs (lines 1242–1273) and the terminal branch (lines 1374–1393) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the scoped walk hits the page cap (return code 2), no result is cached and the next poll repeats the full walk. The active-run cache (IMPL_SCOPED_ACTIVE_RUN_ID) is only populated when the walk finds an active run (rc=0, active>0); a capped walk leaves it empty.
  WHY: In a busy repository where the first 1,000 runs in the created=> window are all full, each POLL_INTERVAL-second poll issues up to SCOPED_RUN_LOOKUP_MAX_PAGES (default 10) API calls until PHASE_TIMEOUT expires. With a 10-second poll interval, that is up to 60 GitHub API requests per minute consumed by a single smoke-test run, drawn from the shared rate-limit budget. The pass-1 finding's claim that "ongoing changes to the page-1 run state can reset the inactivity timer" is not correct — LAST_ACTIVITY is updated by run-state progress, not by the walk itself — but the repeated-walk cost is real. The edge case is rare (requires 1,000+ runs in the window) and the wait is still bounded by PHASE_TIMEOUT, so severity is low.
